creation.title: Create character
creation.intro: Pick a race and background — base ability scores come from the background table. Roll your racial dice and enter the results as Correction.
creation.name: Name
creation.correctionOutOfRange: Correction is outside what the racial dice can roll: {{list}}
creation.rollsOwnSplit: This background rolls its own Skill/Body/Mind instead of listing fixed values — enter what you rolled.
creation.pointBuyHint: Optional (Epic Treasury p. 64): pick each value instead of rolling it. Every pick has a point cost shown next to it — the six Ability corrections must total 0 or less, and a rolled Skill/Body/Mind totals separately.

sheet.fellowIntro: Optional (Core Rulebook I, pp. 192-202): a simplified, damage-immune version of this PC for another play group to borrow as a guest NPC. Name, race, gender, age, level, MP and classes are read straight off the sheet above.
sheet.noFellowActions: No actions on the table yet — a Fellow can only do what is listed here.
sheet.noRiderClass: No Rider levels — only Horse, War Horse, Mini Manabike and Manabike can be ridden.
sheet.mountVariantsNote: Bought with reputation for +5 movement, no rental: {{names}}.
sheet.mountCatalogNote: {{count}} mounts from Core Rulebook III. A mount from another book is typed in by hand.
sheet.schoolsNote: Entry to a School and each of its Secrets is bought separately with Reputation (usually 50 to join, then each Secret's own cost) — the sheet does not track a Reputation budget, the same as every other Reputation purchase.
sheet.workSkillsIntro: Optional (Epic Treasury pp. 65-68, Raxia Life pp. 47-108): non-adventuring professions, used for out-of-combat checks. Guideline for a new PC: 5 levels per skill, 10 levels total — not enforced, a bookkeeping reminder. A level, once taken, is never lost.

reference.title: Reference
reference.intro: Everything the books settle before you roll: correction dice, what a class costs and what each catalog holds.

classDescription.fighter: Heavy weapons and armour — the party's front line and its main damage dealer.
classDescription.grappler: Wrestling and unarmed combat; Chain Attack; its own weapon category; wears the same armour as a Fencer.
classDescription.fencer: A finesse fighter: halves a weapon's Required Strength (rounded up) and crits more often with any weapon.
classDescription.marksman: Ranged combat; unlike the other warrior classes its level does not add to Evasion.
classDescription.battle-dancer: +1 Evasion, Accuracy and damage per level; dance manoeuvres; Grappler weapons and armour; an extra feat from a short list at level 1.
classDescription.sorcerer: The damage school: spells arrive on their own with each level (~4 per level); needs a voice and free hands.
classDescription.conjurer: Summoning and puppet animation for scouting, undead and golems at higher levels; focuses through a magical artefact.
classDescription.priest: Healing, turning undead and blessings; you pick a deity when you take the class; focuses through a Holy Symbol.
classDescription.artificer: Magitech: magispheres become tools; the only class with guns and bullets; focuses through a magisphere of the right size.
classDescription.fairy-tamer: Calls fairies through gems by colour and type — earth, fire, water, wind, light, dark and 'fairy'; movement is limited while casting.
classDescription.druid: Calls the spirits of nature, ~59 spells; Symbols of Beneficence give powerful once-a-day blessings.
classDescription.daemonologist: Gate Imp and Abyss Gate: summons and banishes daemons through the Daemon Action Chart, ~46 spells.
classDescription.abyss-gazer: ~27 spells with an Enhancement system — an extra effect paid for with Daemon's Blood or an Abyss Shard. A separate class, not a Daemonologist under another name.
classDescription.bibliomancer: Spells are bought and found one at a time rather than granted by level, then prepared into a grimoire through slots.
classDescription.scout: Initiative: the class level is added to the roll. Perception: hidden threats, danger sense, locks, pockets, disguise and traps.
classDescription.ranger: Herbalism, first aid, survival and knowledge of terrain.
classDescription.sage: Monster knowledge and the weak points that come with it, plus general knowledge, research and appraisal.
classDescription.enhancer: Techniques: physical enhancement of the body — the Bard's trick turned on yourself.
classDescription.bard: Spellsongs in combat, rhythm banked as a resource, and Finales that spend it.
classDescription.rider: Handles a mount (animal, mythical beast or magitech), ~30 stunts, hired through the Rider's Guild. Riding rolls AGI; finding a mount's weak point rolls INT.
classDescription.alchemist: Evocations (~28 of them, and not magic) are paid for with Material Cards instead of MP: five colours across four ranks.
classDescription.tactician: Stratagems buff allies without spending MP and bank Edge, which pays for personal Maneuvers. Needs a voice and a Strategist Insignia.
classDescription.geomancer: A Geograph banks Qi points that turn into Aspects — a random effect over a zone; no MP, a Minor Action.
classDescription.heritor: Only helps characters with multiple sections — Diablos, Drakes, Basilisks, Scissorscorpions — whose other sections it drives: one Infusion per level, plus Defense, Max HP and Max MP for those sections. Barbarous Rage, a book outside files/; those races are not in the catalog yet.
classDescription.dark-hunter: Essence Weavings (28 of them): steering thrown weapons and buffing yourself at the cost of HP. Mental Power = class level + SPR modifier.

reference.vagrantSystem: Created with the Vagrant system instead of correction dice
reference.missingData: Dice pending a sourcebook the project does not have
reference.racesNote: Correction dice with the span each one can roll, plus what a race forbids and what it grants.
reference.classesNote: A level of a Major class costs more than a Minor one at every step — the tables below are the whole price list.
reference.backgroundsNote: What each roll on a race table hands you: a starting class, a Skill/Body/Mind split and the XP you begin with.
reference.spellsNote: Every spell the research covers, by school. Schools with no per-spell list in the books are missing on purpose.
reference.featsNote: Core I and Core II. Core III adds more that the research has not reached yet.
reference.artsNote: The Enhancer’s Techniques and the Bard’s Spellsongs and Finales, with the class level each one needs.
reference.itemsNote: What the Magic Guild can burn into a weapon, and the 36 curses that come with it.
reference.abyssSkillsNote: A powerful named ability instead of a typical enhancement — same procedure and price, but the curse comes from the Additional Abyss Curse Table below (Abyss Breaker, pp. 44-46).
reference.evocationsNote: The Alchemist’s Evocations: the class level each one needs and the Material Cards it burns. Card rank is chosen at the table and sets how strong the effect is.
reference.equipmentNote: Weapons, armor and shields added by Core Rulebook III. The Core I and II shop is not in the catalog — those items are typed in by hand.
reference.weaponLine: Stance / Min STR / Acc. / Power / Crit / Add'l
reference.mountsNote: Every mount Core Rulebook III gives a data block, level by level, plus mount armaments and the items that carry or repair one.
reference.geomancerNote: All 27 Domain Aspects (Magus Arts pp. 24-27), by required Geomancer level and domain, plus the nine Geographs needed to use them.
reference.tacticianNote: All 35 Stratagems and 15 Maneuvers (Magus Arts pp. 36-41), by required Tactician level, with the Rank, Type and Edge cost/gain each one prints.
reference.essenceWeavingsNote: All 28 Essence Weavings (Abyss Breaker pp. 29-35), by required Dark Hunter level, with the Type, HP Cost and prerequisite each one prints.
reference.schoolsNote: All 18 Battle Mastery Schools (pp. 44-77) with their School Equipment and all 64 Secrets, grouped by school. Dikehorn Twin Ice Spirit Technique grants Reputation-bought Conjurer spells instead of Secrets — see its note.
reference.workSkillsNote: All 81 work skills Raxia Life lists, by the book's own six categories. Only the name, profession and book page are catalogued — the checks and level bonuses stay in the book.
reference.treasureDropNote: A GM tool (Epic Treasury pp. 69-75), not a character feature: spend Treasure Points to give a monster combat abilities, then roll the matching table for the loot it drops. An item a player actually gets goes into their Inventory by hand, like anything bought at a shop.
reference.adventurerLevelTotal: Total of the PCs' Adventurer Levels
reference.vagrantNote: An alternative character-creation system for a non-adventurer PC (Outlaw Profile Book, Part 1). Pick a Category and Type instead of a free class pick, then roll the Childhood and Adolescent Experience tables for that race instead of the racial correction dice. Nothing here is wired into character creation — read the numbers here and enter them on the sheet by hand, the same way Work Skills and Treasure Drop are reference-only.
reference.vagrantChildhoodNote: Replaces the racial A-F correction dice: pick a race and Category, roll 1d66 (1d6 for five tables marked D6), and use the printed Ability Score Correction as-is.
reference.advancedCombatNote: A GM ruleset for running combat on a real 2D battlefield (Epic Treasury pp. 78-91) instead of the abstract melee/independent bookkeeping of Simplified and Standard Combat. Nothing here describes a character — only how the GM manages positions, movement and range in meters. Four small lookup tables exist in the whole section; everything else is procedure to run at the table.
